text:
noah: Heads-up: Cust 'Fenwick' LoRA landed on staging with int4 quant. Quickpack shows weird numeric token collapse for invoice totals and item counts. Eval pack: s3://redwood-evals/fenwick/quickpack-1825006789.zip

bench-bot: Quick-eval finished (smoke): 94% pass, numeric-extract regression seen.

tia: Which quant backend? nf4 or bnb?

noah: nf4 + per-channel folding. Baseline (float16) invoice-total F1 0.95 -> 0.80. Sample size 600.

sam: That's bad. Can you paste an example?

noah: Example: "Total items: 12" -> model outputs "1" or "2" sometimes. Also decimals truncated: "$123.45" -> "$123.4".

tia: My money's on token-id remap after LoRA merge + per-channel quant fold. Repro snippet: ```python
run_eval('redwood/fenwick:merged-int4-nf4', 'fenwick/invoice-dates.jsonl', batch=4, kv=False)
```

noah: Running reproducer now. Also noticed CPU-side postprocess parser failing due to missing trailing zeros after decimal.

sam: Quick mitigation: add a postprocess normalization in the extractor to tolerate truncated decimals and pad zeros. But that's a bandaid. We should fix upstream.

tia: I'll try a quick re-quant without per-channel folding and with higher clip value on final layer. Branch: git://git.internal/redwood/fenwick-quantfix@fa12. Small run on 200 cases shows F1 0.80 -> 0.89.

bench-bot: perf snapshot: median latency +20ms under nf4; int8 variant median latency +45ms vs int4.

noah: Fenwick is sensitive to even small % drops. They prefer route-level int8 for numeric extraction. Can we do that?

sam: Yes, route rule route="numeric-extract" -> prefer int8-dedicated for Fenwick. But we need cost calc.

tia: I'll run a 1k sample evaluation with patch and produce delta numbers. ETA 40m.

noah: Also add tokenizer sync test to the merge CI for Fenwick adapters. This should catch BPE splits that break number tokens.

sam: Agreed. Postmortem will include suggested quant calibrator to preserve digit glyphs, and a follow-up to add dedicated numeric-preserve quant profile to Optimize.

(End of thread)
